problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}-x\, & \text{ for }\,x\le -1 \\ x+c\, & \text{ for }\,x>-1\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to -1}f(x)=1.$ What is the value of the constant $c?$
worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to -1}f(x)$ to be equal to $1,$ the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal to $1.$

- Approaching from the left, we have $x<-1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=-x.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}(-x) \\  & =-(-1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>-1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=x+c.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}(x+c) \\  & =-1+c.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}f(x) \\ 1 & =-1+c \\ c & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
